interface-management.title: INTERFACE MANAGEMENT
content: Policy Ref. MAH-ENC-INT-OP-POL-001  ·  Projects Interface Management Procedure

interface-management.title: Purpose & Governing Principles
content: Why this procedure exists and the rules that are never negotiable

interface-management.title: 01 · PURPOSE
content: This procedure sets the framework for identifying, classifying, managing and closing interface points across all MAH E&C projects — preventing design conflicts, construction delays and cost overruns.
Identify, classify and document every interface point in the Interface Points Register.
Give every interface a named owner, a target date and a resolution route.
Hold coordination meetings, progress updates and resolution workshops.
Track each point in a formal system until it is verified by all parties.
Capture lessons learned and feed them into future phases and projects.

interface-management.title: 01 · NON-NEGOTIABLES
content: No interface point exists outside the Interface Points Register — each one has an owner and a target date.
No verbal-only coordination: every decision is recorded in MoM, RFI, transmittal or Aconex.
No interface point is closed without evidence and sign-off by all concerned parties.
No issue stays unresolved beyond its target date without formal escalation.
Authority coordination goes through the GRO, with a valid Client authorization letter.
Escalation is fact-based and used when coordination fails — it never replaces coordination.
Safety-related interface issues may be escalated immediately to any level, regardless of hierarchy.

interface-management.title: Definitions & Interface Types
content: What an interface point is and where interfaces arise

interface-management.title: 02 · DEFINITIONS
content: A location, activity or information flow where two or more parties, systems or scopes meet and require coordination. The Interface Owner is the person or department assigned to manage and close it.
Physical: scopes meet on site (clashes, crossings, tie-ins). Functional: systems must integrate. Organizational: a responsibility boundary between parties (battery limits).
Minimizes risk and design / construction conflicts, avoids delays and cost overruns, optimizes resources and supports timely decisions and stakeholder alignment.

interface-management.title: 02 · INTERFACE TYPES
content: •  Engineering ↔ Construction, Planning ↔ Procurement, QA/QC ↔ Site, HSE ↔ concurrent works.
•  Design data release, shop drawings, inspections, NCRs, schedule, budget and Aconex transmittals.
•  Client, PMC / Consultant, subcontractors, vendors, authorities, utilities and adjacent contractors.
•  Approvals, IFC / as-built reviews, work-area handover, permits, NOCs and final acceptance.
•  Dedicated coordination meeting: Planning, Technical, PM, Procurement, QA/QC, HSE, Interface.
•  Joint Responsibility Matrix signed by both parties; no deviation without formal re-issue.

interface-management.title: 02 · PROJECT LIFE CYCLE
content: Interfaces Across the Project Life Cycle
Scope boundaries, package overlaps, discipline clashes, IFC revisions and data release.
Long-lead items vs design freeze, vendor approvals and material handover points.
Work-zone handover, sequencing, site clashes and authority dependencies.
System integration, as-builts, final approvals, NOCs and acceptance.

interface-management.title: Roles & Responsibilities
content: Who owns what — from the E&C Sector down to subcontractors

interface-management.title: 03 · ROLES
content: Approves Interface Management Plans, Registers and Issue Logs.
Receives Level 2 escalations on schedule, cost, quality or safety.
Escalates critical issues to the VP E&C Sector.
Ensures alignment and collaboration across all project teams.
Approves resolutions with cost or schedule impact; supports escalation.
Ensures every interface decision is documented and implemented on site.
Develops and maintains the Interface Register, Matrix and Issue Log.
Chairs coordination meetings; issues MoM within 48 hours; tracks RFIs.
Coordinates Client, PMC and authorities (via GRO); reports and escalates.

interface-management.title: 03 · ROLES
content: Reviews IFC drawings to identify interface points between trades.
Answers interface RFIs; issues integrated drawings and as-built data.
Keeps a record of all technical coordination outcomes.
Coordinates field activities of disciplines working in adjacent zones.
Keeps sequences within agreed interface boundaries and dates.
Reports site clashes at once; implements and documents resolutions.
Integrates interface milestones into the master schedule and look-ahead.
Treats permits, NOCs and third-party dependencies as predecessors.
Alerts the Interface Manager early to schedule risks.

interface-management.title: 03 · ROLES
content: Verifies interface compliance, inspects zones before handover, issues and closes NCRs.
Controls safety where operations overlap; delivers awareness sessions and records.
Verifies boundaries and control points; joint surveys and as-built data for closure.
Aligns deliveries with resolution plans; defines handover points in packages.
Supports VOs and claims; issues timely contractual notices.
Liaises with MOT, Municipality, SEC, NWC, Civil Defense for permits and NOCs.
Attend meetings, submit shop drawings of connection points, keep to boundaries.
Approve resolutions and major decisions; review monthly interface reports.

interface-management.title: 03 · RACI
content: R Responsible · A Accountable · C Consulted · I Informed · A/R Accountable & Responsible  —  Source: MAH-ENC-CNS-PM-TMP-001 Interface Management RACI Matrix

interface-management.title: Process Flow, Meetings & Tools
content: How every interface point moves from identification to verified closure

interface-management.title: 04 · PROCESS FLOW
content: An interface point stays open until it is verified and signed off by all concerned stakeholders. Closure evidence is filed in Aconex; points past their target date are formally escalated.

interface-management.title: 04 · COMMUNICATION
content: Once — agree roles, templates, reporting and communication flow
Coordination: review new, open and closed points; agree actions
Interface review: closure rate and key risks with management / Client
Special meeting for urgent items affecting progress, approvals or safety
Verified and signed off by all parties; evidence in Aconex.
Under review: resolution agreed — awaiting verification and sign-off.
Action pending with owner and target date; escalate if overdue.
Register fields: Interface ID · description · location / zone · originator & receiver discipline · type · required action / responsibility · target date · status · remarks.
Finish in Interface and still not finish for construction work.

interface-management.title: 04 · TOOLS
content: •  Maps who interfaces with whom, on what scope and where boundaries lie.
•  Built early; updated monthly or whenever scopes or packages change.
•  Tracks every coordination point: owner, target date and status.
•  Updated weekly, after every coordination meeting.
•  Records conflicts affecting progress, cost or safety and how they were resolved.
•  Basis for contractual notices, claims and risk monitoring.

interface-management.title: Escalation, Integration & KPIs
content: Time-bound escalation and how we measure interface performance

interface-management.title: 05 · ESCALATION
content: Issue unresolved after the coordination meeting, or affecting short-term activities. Interface Manager escalates to the Project Manager — response within 2–5 working days.
Issue impacting schedule, cost, quality or safety. Project Manager escalates to the Projects Director / Head of Interface — response within 5–8 working days.
Critical issue affecting milestones, contract obligations or program objectives. Projects Director escalates to the VP E&C Sector — immediate instructions and decision.

interface-management.title: 05 · ESCALATION
content: Routine issue: Interface Manager follows up with the Consultant / Subcontractor (3–5 working days); if progress is affected, the PM escalates to the PMC Team Leader.
Issue impacting milestones, approvals or permits: the Project Manager escalates to the Client / Employer Representative — response within 7–14 working days.
Critical issue on permits, NOCs or statutory compliance: Project Director / GRO escalate to the Authority or Client senior management — immediately / as required.

interface-management.title: 05 · INTEGRATION
content: Interface milestones sit in the master schedule and look-ahead. Permits, NOCs and third-party dependencies are predecessors of critical activities.
Every interface point is a potential risk or opportunity (ISO 31000). Critical interfaces are linked to the Risk Register with mitigation actions and owners.
Escalation is fact-based and time-bound, supported by drawings, schedules and correspondence. The Contract & Claims Manager issues timely notices to protect our rights.

interface-management.title: 05 · MONITORING
content: Interface points with owner & target date
Interface points closed by target date
Closures with evidence & sign-off in Aconex

interface-management.title: Assets, Awareness & Closeout
content: Protecting what is not ours and keeping every team aligned

interface-management.title: 06 · THIRD-PARTY ASSETS
content: Damage to Third-Party Assets — Prevent & Respond
Prevention: utility detection and trial pits, marking, PTW, RA/JSA, toolbox talks, certified equipment, competent operators, supervision and coordination with utility owners.
*Work resumes only after written approval from Project Management. External communication (utility owners, authorities, Civil Defense, Police, media) by authorized management only.
•  Public, private or critical infrastructure damage

interface-management.title: 06 · AWARENESS & CLOSURE
content: Quarterly awareness sessions — plus after phase changes, new subcontractors or incidents.
HSE Manager delivers sessions and records attendance; PM ensures full participation.
Avoid: verbal-only coordination, no owner or date, no follow-up, closure without evidence.
Best practice: register at once, assign an owner, update weekly, close with evidence.
Records retained for the contract period or project duration + 1 year.
No interface point is closed until it is verified, evidenced in Aconex and signed off by all parties.
MAH manages interfaces as an integrated project-control function — identified early, owned, tracked and closed with evidence.
Management provides the leadership, resources and guidance to apply this policy on every E&C project — minimizing risks, avoiding delays and optimizing resources.

stakeholder-management.title: Purpose & Policy Principles
content: Why this procedure exists and the rules that are never negotiable

stakeholder-management.title: 01 · PURPOSE
content: This procedure sets a structured framework to identify, analyse, engage and communicate with internal and external stakeholders in every project phase — so expectations, concerns and inputs are recorded and addressed systematically.
Identify all internal and external stakeholders at project start and record them in the Stakeholder Register.
Assess power and interest with the Power–Interest Matrix to set each stakeholder's engagement priority.
Run the Engagement Plan: coordination meetings, authority follow-ups, workshops and progress updates.
Track approvals, influence and engagement status; report monthly through KPIs and dashboards.
Capture lessons learned at close-out and feed them into future MAH projects.

stakeholder-management.title: 01 · NON-NEGOTIABLES
content: Every stakeholder is in the Stakeholder Register with an owner, a category and an engagement priority.
No verbal-only commitments: every agreement is recorded in MoM, letter, transmittal or Aconex.
No commitment beyond delegated authority — escalate and obtain approval before confirming.
Governance first: stakeholder satisfaction never overrides policy, contract or statutory compliance.
Authority engagement goes through the GRO, with valid authorization letters.
No stakeholder issue is closed without evidence and sign-off by all concerned parties.
Policy deviations are exceptions only — justified, executive-approved, time-bound and recorded.

stakeholder-management.title: Stakeholders, Categories & Analysis
content: Who our stakeholders are and how we prioritize them

stakeholder-management.title: 02 · DEFINITIONS
content: Any internal or external party that has an impact on, or may be affected by, project activities — from MAH departments and project teams to the Client, consultants, authorities, subcontractors, community and service providers.

The SR is the controlled list of all stakeholders with influence / interest levels, communication plan and actions. The SEP sets communication frequency, expectations and engagement strategy; the SEP Owner updates and coordinates actions.

The categorization model that sets communication priority: Manage Closely, Keep Satisfied, Keep Informed or Monitor. Also used: SMP – Stakeholder Management Plan · SM – Stakeholder Manager · NOC – No Objection Certificate.

stakeholder-management.title: 02 · CATEGORIES
content: •  MAH management, functional departments, project teams and site staff.
•  Design, planning, QA/QC, HSE, procurement, commercial and contracts.
•  Client / Employer, PMC / consultants, authorities and utility owners.
•  Subcontractors, vendors, service providers and community representatives.
•  Project: Stakeholder Manager, Project Manager, Interface Manager.
•  Program: Projects Director · Sector: VP E&C, PMO and Risk Manager.

stakeholder-management.title: 02 · ANALYSIS
content: KEEP SATISFIED High power · Low interest Targeted updates on decisions that need them Executive management · approving authorities · utility owners
MANAGE CLOSELY High power · High interest Regular meetings and direct coordination Client / Employer · PMC / Consultant · permitting authorities
MONITOR Low power · Low interest Minimal engagement — watch for changes Non-critical suppliers · service providers · general public
KEEP INFORMED Low power · High interest Routine communication and progress updates Subcontractors · internal departments · adjacent contractors · community

stakeholder-management.title: Roles & Responsibilities
content: Who owns what — from the E&C Sector down to subcontractors and the Client

stakeholder-management.title: 03 · ROLES
content: Leads the SMP, Stakeholder Register and Engagement Plan.
Analyses power / interest; chairs meetings; issues MoM in 48 hours.
Tracks KPIs and satisfaction; escalates critical issues.
Integrates stakeholder management into the PEP; allocates resources.
Approves the SMP and strategies affecting scope, cost or schedule.
Attends high-level meetings; decides on escalated issues.
Coordinates interface points with departments, subcontractors, authorities.
Aligns the Interface Register with stakeholder engagement actions.
Supports communication flow; escalates unresolved conflicts.

stakeholder-management.title: 03 · ROLES
content: Reviews IFC drawings for stakeholder requirements and impacts.
Gives timely technical responses to stakeholder comments.
Presents design updates; closes technical actions in meetings.
Puts engagement milestones and commitments into the schedule.
Monitors stakeholder activities; reports delays and dependencies.
Updates dashboards of achieved and pending engagement targets.
Identifies stakeholders linked to obligations, claims and variations.
Keeps all claim-related communication formal and traceable.
Assesses the contractual and financial impact of decisions.

stakeholder-management.title: 03 · ROLES
content: Identify discipline stakeholders, raise emerging issues and close assigned actions.
Addresses stakeholder quality concerns through NCRs and corrective actions.
Aligns vendors and subcontractors on delivery, compliance and schedule.
Keeps commercial communication formal; assesses financial impact.
Coordinates authority attendance and access; follows up permits and NOCs.
Report stakeholders in their scope, attend meetings, meet obligations.
Reviews and approves the SMP; responds on time to contractor letters.
Endorses the approach, approves key strategies, gives timely decisions.

stakeholder-management.title: 03 · RACI
content: R Responsible · A Accountable · C Consulted · I Informed · A/R Accountable & Responsible  —  Source: MAH-ENC-CNS-PM-TMP-002 Stakeholder Management RACI Matrix

stakeholder-management.title: Process, Engagement & Meetings
content: How every stakeholder issue moves from identification to verified closure

stakeholder-management.title: 04 · PROCESS FLOW
content: The Project Manager approves each closure against evidence — approvals, MoMs, drawings, NOCs. If not approved, the issue returns to coordination. All documents are uploaded to Aconex before closure; KPIs and response times are reported to management.

stakeholder-management.title: 04 · PROCESS MAP
content: One Process at Three Management Levels

Identify and register stakeholders, assess them on the Power–Interest Matrix, coordinate through meetings, RFIs and authority follow-ups, resolve through discipline coordination, verify documents in Aconex and close with Project Manager approval.

The Lead Interface Manager consolidates stakeholders affecting several projects and classifies them by program impact; the Projects Director validates; conflicts on schedule, approvals or shared assets are resolved and KPIs reported monthly.

The Lead Stakeholder Manager flags strategic, reputational or corporate risks; the Risk Manager assesses the impact on MAH's image and client relationship; the VP approves mitigation, the PMO monitors it and lessons are captured.

stakeholder-management.title: 04 · ENGAGEMENT PLANNING
content: Method, frequency, responsible person and information to share — aligned with the SR.
Emails, meetings, workshops, transmittals, letters and awareness sessions.
Every communication and feedback in the Communication & Action Tracker.
At each stage change, or when stakeholder roles or needs change.

stakeholder-management.title: 04 · MEETINGS
content: Once — introduce the framework, key stakeholders, roles and reporting
Coordination: review issues, actions and new concerns (or bi-weekly)
Review: engagement performance, open issues and KPI trends with Client / PMC
Special meeting for urgent issues, authority approvals or critical coordination
Actions completed, evidence filed and all parties signed off.
Under review: response agreed — awaiting verification.
Action pending with owner and target date; escalate if overdue.
Meeting deliverables: MoM within 48 hours · updated Stakeholder Register · Action Tracker with target dates · Engagement Dashboard of critical stakeholders and approvals.

stakeholder-management.title: 04 · MEETING AGENDAS
content: •  Attendance, previous MoM, Register updates, new issues and dependencies.
•  Design, schedule, permits / NOCs, risks, RFIs, actions and closure targets.
•  Client, PMC, authorities, subcontractors: open issues and action status.
•  Permits / NOCs via GRO, access, utilities, risks and upcoming submissions.
•  Every issue logged by transmittal, email or MoM; owners acknowledge actions.
•  Overdue items escalated to PM and PMC; approvals linked to the schedule.

stakeholder-management.title: Escalation Matrix & KPIs
content: Six escalation levels with response times — and how we measure engagement

stakeholder-management.title: 05 · ESCALATION MATRIX
content: Response: 1–3 working days. Routine stakeholder issues and minor coordination conflicts, with no policy or contract breach. The Project Manager / Interface Manager engage the stakeholder, clarify scope and constraints, and record the issue in the Stakeholder Register.

Response: 3–5 working days. Issue not resolved at project level, or with potential schedule or cost impact. The Project Manager and discipline leads coordinate internally (Technical, Planning, QA/QC, HSE) and issue a formal response to the stakeholder.

Response: 5–7 working days. Proposed solution conflicts with MAH policy or the contract, or has financial implications. The Contract / Commercial Manager assesses the risks, advises on variations, claims or mitigation and gives a written recommendation.

stakeholder-management.title: 05 · ESCALATION MATRIX
content: Response: 7–10 working days. Multi-project impact, authority-level conflict, or high reputational or delivery risk. The Projects Director leads strategic engagement, cross-project alignment and direct negotiation with the stakeholder.

Response: As required / urgent. Non-compliant external request, critical legal, policy or reputational risk, or deadlock with an authority. Sector Head / Executive Management gives the final decision, communicates authority-to-authority and approves the strategic position.

Response: As required. Legal exposure, regulatory non-compliance or contractual dispute. Legal Counsel / Corporate Governance provide a legal opinion, formal notices or claims, and risk-containment actions.

stakeholder-management.title: 05 · MONITORING
content: Feedback actions closed by target date
KPI dashboard & summary report to management

stakeholder-management.title: Governance, Exceptions & Closeout
content: Decisions within authority, controlled deviations and lessons learned

stakeholder-management.title: 06 · GOVERNANCE PRIORITY
content: Requests are checked against policy, contract, law and HSE / quality / ethics; commitments beyond authority are escalated first.
*MAH never proceeds with a solution that breaches policy, contract, statutory requirements or governance — regardless of external pressure. Decisions go to the Register and Issue & Decision Log.

stakeholder-management.title: 06 · EXCEPTIONS & CLOSURE
content: Exceptions need a formal request: the issue, policy constraint, risks and mitigation.
Written Sector / Executive approval (plus Legal review if needed) before any deviation.
Approved deviations are limited in scope and time and set no precedent.
Awareness and collaboration sessions at key stages, recorded with the HSE and Interface teams.
Lessons learned captured for each exception and at close-out; records archived per document control.
Stakeholder satisfaction never overrides governance compliance.
MAH engages stakeholders early, communicates transparently and decides within authority — identified, analysed, engaged and closed with evidence.
Project Management leadership provides the support, resources and direction to apply this policy on every project — ensuring accountability, transparency and consistency.

comparison.title: INTERFACE MANAGEMENT
content: A comparative analysis of two complementary MAH governance systems
How the Engineering & Construction Sector coordinates technical connection points and stakeholder relationships across project delivery

comparison.title: Agenda
content: Scope and structure, side by side

comparison.title: 01 · THE CORE DISTINCTION
content: Both disciplines coordinate people, but they control different risks
What must connect, align, or close?
Boundaries, dependencies, design integration and field coordination at physical, functional and organizational connection points.
Clashes, handoff gaps, rework and unresolved technical dependencies between disciplines, packages or contractors.
Who can affect the project, and how should we engage them?
Influence, interest and expectations of the people and parties who affect — or are affected by — the project, mapped on a Power–Interest Matrix.
Resistance, non-response, conflicting expectations, reputational impact and policy deviation under external pressure.

comparison.title: 02 · SCOPE AND STRUCTURE
content: The same five dimensions, answered two different ways
An interface point: where scopes, disciplines, organizations or information flows meet.
A stakeholder: any party that affects, or may be affected by, the project.
Flat split: Internal Interface Points vs. External Interface Points.
Power–Interest Matrix: Manage Closely, Keep Satisfied, Keep Informed, Monitor.
Interface Points Register + Interface Matrix Sheet (who interfaces with whom, on what).
Stakeholder Register + Stakeholder Engagement Plan (who matters, how much, how engaged).
Interface Issue Log — escalated conflicts and physical/technical clashes.
Case Feedback Log — escalated conflicts, resistance and unmet expectations.
Interface Manager, supported by discipline engineers and subcontractors.
Stakeholder Manager, supported by the Interface Manager and Department Heads.

comparison.title: 03 · ROLES COMPARISON
content: Connection points, clashes and holding areas — where scopes, systems and work zones physically or contractually meet.
Influence, interest and expectations of the people and parties who affect — or are affected by — the project.
“Where do our works meet, and is every point resolved?”
“Who matters, what do they expect, and are they on board?”
Utility crossings and tie-ins, battery limits, work-zone handovers, shared laydown / holding areas.
Client, PMC, authorities, utility owners, subcontractors, community — approvals, NOCs, concerns.
Interface Issue Log, MoM, RFIs, closure evidence and sign-off in Aconex.
Communication & Action Tracker, MoM, engagement dashboard, lessons learned.
Interface points closed by target date — with evidence and all-party sign-off.
≥85% of stakeholder issues resolved on time; meetings held as scheduled.

Two roles — they cannot be merged into one title:  interfaces need technical and contractual control of points, clashes and holding areas; stakeholders need management of people, influence and expectations. Different skills, tools, registers and procedures (PRO-001 vs PRO-002) — combining them loses one or the other. They work side by side: the Interface Manager closes the technical point, the Stakeholder Manager secures the agreement behind it.

comparison.title: 04 · WHERE THEY INTERSECT
content: Two separate roles — connected, not merged
INTERFACE MANAGER Controls connection points  ·  PRO-001 –  Interface Points Register –  Interface Matrix Sheet –  Design & field coordination –  Technical RFIs and clashes
STAKEHOLDER MANAGER Controls relationships  ·  PRO-002 –  Stakeholder Register –  Power–Interest Matrix –  Engagement & communication plan –  Relationship-level conflicts

ALIGNED, NOT MERGED Each role keeps its own owner, register, RACI and procedure. The Interface Manager supports the Stakeholder Manager’s communication flow, and both registers are aligned after every coordination meeting.

Escalation stays separate but aligned:  interface conflicts follow the PRO-001 escalation route; stakeholder disagreements follow the PRO-002 escalation matrix. Each manager owns his own log — both feed the same governance chain.

comparison.title: 05 · ORGANIZATIONAL SEPARATION
content: Two disciplines, two departments — not one combined role
A technical / engineering function accountable for physical and design coordination across disciplines and contractors.
Interface Manager — owns the Interface Points Register, Interface Matrix Sheet and Interface Issue Log.
Technical coordination gets diluted by negotiation and relationship demands, slowing clash resolution and design sign-off.
A commercial function accountable for client, authority and stakeholder engagement and communication.
Stakeholder Manager — owns the Stakeholder Register, Power–Interest Matrix and Engagement Plan.
Stakeholder engagement gets diluted by day-to-day technical firefighting, weakening client and authority relationships.

Recommendation:  keep Interface Management and Stakeholder Management as two separate departments, each with its own manager, register and RACI ownership. The Interface Manager should act only as the coordination bridge between them (see previous slide) — not as a merged role carrying both mandates.

comparison.title: SUMMARY
content: Two separate roles on the same delivery risk — connected, never merged

Different roles, different owners The Interface Manager controls connection points; the Stakeholder Manager controls relationships. Each has its own register, matrix, RACI and procedure (PRO-001 / PRO-002) — they cannot be merged into one title.

Aligned, not combined The Interface Manager supports the Stakeholder Manager’s communication flow, and both registers are aligned after every coordination meeting — two accountable owners, one coordinated picture.

Escalate to the right depth Route technical clashes through the 3-level interface escalation; route relationship, contractual or reputational issues onto the 6-level stakeholder matrix, up to Legal / Corporate Governance.

comparison.title: 10 · DOCUMENT BASIS
content: This comparison is drawn from four controlled MAH documents

Reference note:  all four documents were checked and approved by the same governance chain — Projects Director, Head of HSE & TMO, Head of QA/QC and VP Engineering & Construction Sector — confirming this comparison rests on a single, coordinated set of controlled documents.

logistics.title: LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT
content: Procedures, Roles & Site Interfaces  —  Team Briefing

logistics.title: Purpose & Governing Principles
content: Why this procedure exists and the rules that are never negotiable

logistics.title: 01 · PURPOSE
content: This procedure establishes the mandatory framework for planning, approving, coordinating, executing, monitoring and closing logistics activities across MG / E&C construction and infrastructure projects.
Safeguard project schedule, cost, quality and HSE performance.
Prevent congestion, double handling, idle resources and workfront disruption.
Maintain safe public traffic, property, pedestrian and emergency access.
Control logistics interfaces with suppliers, subcontractors, authorities and adjacent stakeholders.
Require every project to prepare a project-specific Logistics Management Plan (LMP).

logistics.title: 01 · NON-NEGOTIABLES
content: No logistics activity proceeds without an approved requirement, owner and confirmed workfront.
No mobilization before the applicable mobilization gate has been satisfied.
No live-traffic movement without TMP controls and Traffic / HSE confirmation.
No abnormal load without route verification, permits and escorts.
Materials are traceable from purchase and dispatch through receipt, storage and installation.
Any deviation is risk-assessed, approved and recorded before implementation.
Every person in logistics operations has authority to stop an unsafe or unauthorized movement.

logistics.title: Roles & Responsibilities
content: Who owns what across leadership, site execution and support functions

logistics.title: 02 · ROLES
content: Approves logistics strategy and major resources.
Resolves escalated constraints affecting milestones, cost or stakeholders.
Ensures coordination across projects sharing resources or routes.
Approves the project LMP before operations commence.
Chairs or delegates the weekly logistics coordination meeting.
Reviews KPI performance, risks and unresolved corrective actions.
Develops, implements and maintains the project LMP.
Manages access routes, gates, delivery schedules and logistics zones.
Authorized to stop or reschedule any unsafe or unapproved movement.

logistics.title: 02 · ROLES
content: Confirms workfront readiness and material demand.
Provides construction sequencing and short-term priorities.
Nominates unloading points and responsible receiving personnel.
Implements the approved LMP and daily logistics programme.
Verifies bookings, permits, driver and vehicle documents.
Coordinates with Construction, Stores, HSE, Traffic and Security.
Directs daily activities of workers, drivers and banksmen.
Runs toolbox talks and controls vehicle movement on site.
Reports damaged materials, unsafe conditions and delays immediately.

logistics.title: 02 · ROLES
content: Integrates logistics into the baseline schedule and rolling look-ahead.
Aligns PO dates, confirms supplier readiness and transport arrangements.
Controls receiving documentation, quarantine and rejected materials.
Defines inspection requirements and controls nonconforming materials.
Reviews risk assessments, JHAs, PTWs and verifies compliance.
Stages TMP approvals, route design and traffic-switch controls.
Controls gate access, ID checks and vehicle authorization.
Coordinates authorities, utilities and cross-functional integration.

logistics.title: Approval Gates & Delivery Process
content: The control points and workflow every delivery must pass through

logistics.title: 03 · APPROVAL GATES
content: No gate may be bypassed through verbal instruction. Emergency deviations must be documented and approved by authorized management and HSE representatives.

logistics.title: 03 · DELIVERY PROCESS
content: Construction & Planning issue rolling material and equipment demand.
PO reference, driver/vehicle details, load data and required permits.
Logistics verifies workfront, route, storage and manpower availability.
Security, HSE, QA/QC and Stores clear, receive and record the delivery.

logistics.title: Site Operations Control
content: Managing materials, storage, traffic and equipment day to day

logistics.title: 04 · SITE OPERATIONS
content: •  Ready-mix concrete, asphalt, aggregates and backfill coordinated for direct use.
•  Workfront readiness, mix approval, supplier availability confirmed before dispatch.
•  Zoning plan covers inventory, structural steel, hazardous materials and waste.
•  Rejected and quarantined materials are segregated from active stock.
•  Detarping, concrete sampling/washout, wheel-wash and vehicle holding areas.
•  Each station has approved layout, signage, lighting and inspection schedule.

logistics.title: 04 · SITE OPERATIONS
content: No movement affecting live traffic proceeds until Traffic Management confirms controls: segregated routes, marshals, barriers, signage and continuous emergency access.
Mobilized per the approved histogram. Route geometry, ground bearing capacity, permits, lifting plan, JHA and PTW verified before movement.
Movement from stores/laydown to workfronts is controlled by an approved issue or transfer request, minimizing double handling and blocked access.

logistics.title: Communication, KPIs & Escalation
content: How the team stays aligned and how performance is measured

logistics.title: 05 · COMMUNICATION
content: Logistics look-ahead + interface and permit review
Advance coordination for critical lifts or abnormal loads
No effect on the approved sequence.
Milestone, safety, authority or traffic impact — immediate escalation.
Register fields: issue & location · affected activity/milestone · responsible party · required decision · target closure date · status · escalation level.

logistics.title: Risk, Nonconformance & Closeout
content: Staying ahead of disruption and closing the project out cleanly

logistics.title: 06 · CONTROL
content: Controls: alternative suppliers, backup routes, buffer stock, off-peak delivery, standby lifting equipment, early authority engagement.
Repeated or serious nonconformities are escalated to the Project Manager and HSE Manager and may result in suspension of the supplier or transporter.

logistics.title: 06 · CLOSEOUT
content: Removal of temporary facilities, stations and utilities.
Equipment, vehicle and asset demobilization and reconciliation.
Reinstatement of temporary diversions and laydown areas.
Permit and authority closeout, record handover and archive.
No logistics area is handed over until it is inspected, cleared, reinstated and formally accepted.
MAH manages logistics as an integrated project-control function — not merely a transportation service.
Successful logistics requires coordinated planning between Procurement, Stores, Construction, Planning, HSE, QA/QC, Traffic Management, Security, Interface Management, suppliers and subcontractors.
